title: Social Influence & Addiction
description: Explore conformity without direct coercion through dialogue, evidence and psychological reasoning.

lessons.title: Nobody asked, but everyone does it
lessons.teach: Follow the conversation one message at a time. Notice what the behaviour might be achieving before you decide why it happened. About five minutes.
lessons.objective: Distinguish observable evidence from a tentative explanation of conformity without direct coercion.

nodes.title: What might be happening?
nodes.body:
Descriptive norms are beliefs about what people usually do. They can influence a decision even without an explicit request. The social wish to fit in may combine with curiosity, while nicotine exposure introduces a possible risk of dependence that makes an initial choice consequential.

Observing others does not prove conformity. Preferences, prior use and the group's actual response to refusal matter.
nodes.sources: Bandura (1977), Social Learning Theory; social-norm influence literature; WHO nicotine dependence resources.

nodes.prompt: The goal is to improve the situation without pretending that you can read the person's mind.
nodes.explanation: A proportionate response deals with the actual situation: Decide what you want independently; if offered, decline without needing a complicated justification. Its value does not depend on the other person accepting an interpretation of their motives.

nodes.title: One distinction to keep
nodes.prompt: Fill the missing word: An explanation of what a behaviour might achieve is a working ______, not a proven fact.
nodes.explanation: A hypothesis is an explanation that can be revised when observations fail to support it. This keeps psychological reasoning useful rather than turning it into confident mind-reading.
nodes.counterexample: Observing others does not prove conformity. Preferences, prior use and the group's actual response to refusal matter.
nodes.sources: Bandura (1977), Social Learning Theory; social-norm influence literature; WHO nicotine dependence resources.
